A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GAPT research. All 17 pages of v1 and 22 pages of v3, including equations, figures, tables and appendices, support comparison. The existing material is retained, with additions concentrated in Appendix C.

before.justification: v1 reports original fixed-melody and model-to-model experiments, a study with 12 musicians, and supplementary quantitative results.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds seed comparisons, ablations, training diagnostics and longer-sequence evaluations.

M1.justification: The primary PPO-based GAPT method and two-phase discriminator schedule remain unchanged. Sections C.10-C.13 add evaluated variants using Dr.GRPO, a melody-conditioned discriminator, and extended-context or sliding-window inference. These are auxiliary procedural extensions rather than replacements of the main method.

E1.justification: The datasets and existing interaction tasks are retained. Section C.13 adds an explicit fixed-melody extrapolation scenario using sequences of at least 512 frames, beyond the 256-frame training horizon, on the existing test corpora and Wikifonia.

E2.justification: Table 8 adds GRPO with and without adversarial training; the text specifies a Dr.GRPO implementation. Table 9 adds GAPT with a discriminator conditioned on both melody and chords. The original Online MLE, ReaLchords and non-adversarial GAPT comparisons remain.

E3.justification: The added experiments substantially extend the evaluation design through reward-weight controls, alternative RL optimization and discriminator-input comparisons. Section C.13 evaluates 137 test sequences and 300 Wikifonia sequences using 512-frame context versus a 256-frame sliding window with an eight-frame hop. Table 10 adds average chord pitch-class count as a diagnostic measure. Existing protocols are retained.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's adversarial-removal ablation, embedding visualization and key-shift probe, v3 adds reward-weight and penalty ablations, optimizer and discriminator-input comparisons, training and critic diagnostics, a check for dense-chord metric gaming, and long-sequence robustness analysis. These examine several previously untested design choices and failure conditions.

E5.justification: Section C.7 and Table 6 newly report means and standard deviations across three RL post-training seeds for GAPT, its non-adversarial ablation and ReaLchords on both dataset settings. This adds policy-training uncertainty to central quantitative comparisons. v1 already reported user-study standard errors and paired tests, but not this seed variability; an increase from a previously specified run count is not established.

E6.justification: Existing results remain unchanged, while Tables 6-10 and Figures 8-12 add substantial numerical and qualitative evidence. For example, the new Table 8 reports test harmony/diversity of 0.459/16.872 for GRPO without adversarial training and 0.478/26.603 with it. These are newly reported experimental comparisons, not improvements to previously reported same-setting scores.

T1.justification: Equation 7 introduces a limited mathematical extension by parameterizing the previously equal-weight three-component reward with separate coefficients for the ablations. The original online factorizations, assumptions and adversarial reward definition remain unchanged, and no new proofs or theoretical guarantees are supplied.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution statements and conclusion retain the same claims about mitigating reward hacking, preserving diversity and improving live accompaniment. The appendix adds support without redefining those core contributions.

C2.justification: The appendix substantially expands interpretation of mechanisms and failure conditions. It discusses why excessive rule weighting can reduce coverage, why excessive adversarial weighting can weaken melody alignment, and why removing penalties permits invalid outputs. It also introduces a conditional-discriminator overfitting hypothesis and interpretations of critic tracking, chord-density checks and longer-sequence behavior.

D1.justification: Section C.8 newly discloses eight gradient updates per discriminator step and how training logs are averaged. Sections C.12-C.13 document the shared 2,821-symbol chord vocabulary, provide a vocabulary link, and specify long-sequence inference details. Existing architecture, training hyperparameters and release information are retained.

R1.justification: Section C.10 newly discusses GRPO and Dr.GRPO and positions the adversarial-training benefit across alternative RL objectives. This is a limited extension: the existing related-work section and bibliography are unchanged, and the new algorithms' citations remain unresolved question-mark placeholders.

P1.justification: The existing prose and section organization are essentially unchanged. v3 appends Sections C.7-C.13 with accompanying explanations and expands one author's name from Teng Ma to Aleksandra Teng Ma. There is no extensive rewriting or reorganization of the retained narrative.

P2.justification: v3 substantially expands the visual presentation with a seed-summary table, ablation and chord-density tables, multi-panel training diagnostics, critic plots and long-sequence curves. Tables 8-9 redisplay original Table 1 results alongside new variants. Existing figures and tables are retained without substantive redesign.

improvement.justification: v1 lacked policy-seed uncertainty and systematic tests of several important design choices. v3 addresses these gaps through Table 6 and the reward, optimizer and discriminator ablations in Tables 7-9, while checking potential metric gaming and behavior beyond the training horizon. These additions substantially strengthen the empirical support and clarify failure conditions without removing existing evidence. The unresolved GRPO citations are a limited drawback.
